title: Attacks 2 and 9, retest of P3-RT-05-09: eight controls that their own press makes inactive still take the HTML disabled attribute or leave the page, so keyboard focus falls to <body>
location: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1198 (rotateReset disabled={!api.hydrated || rotation === null}) and :996-1003 (drawOrbit inside {#if orbit.kind === 'wait'}); T02OrbitGarden.svelte:639-640 (grow disabled={!growable}, showTotal disabled={totalShown}); T07SymbolicGame.svelte:525 (table button disabled={... || !canAct[p]}); T05NumbersGameLab.svelte:729-730 (stepB, playToEndB disabled={... || curB().gameOver}); board/BoardEditor.svelte:364-365 (addNode, removeNode disabled={off || reason !== ''}); lesson/Challenge.svelte:107-108 (input and Check disabled={!hydrated || met})
claim: The aria-disabled remedy recorded in RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict and RT-FIX-P3-residual-tools reached only the controls it lists. Eight other controls lose the focus to the document when the reader's own press makes them inactive.
expected: DECISIONS.md, RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: 'after hydration a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus'. SPEC 7.5 A-1 (WCAG 2.4.3). After the press, document.activeElement is the pressed control or another element inside the tool.
observed:
document.activeElement is BODY after Enter on each of these:
- T10 'No rotation' (/tools/geometry/?g=D4, after Rotate +10).
- T10 'Draw the orbit' (/tools/geometry/?g=E8&r=0.1.0.0.0.0.0.0).
- T2 'Show total' (/tools/garden/).
- T2 'Grow one layer' at the last layer.
- T7 table button 'Fire node 1' (/tools/symbolic/, data-moves 1). Every legal fire makes the fired node non-positive, so T7's A-10 table view loses the focus after nearly every move.
- T5 'Play B to the end' (/modules/m4-numbers/ b3, after Reset B).

reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-ownpress-focus.spec.ts (8 tests fail). In this container PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed at the scratch browsers, and a copy of playwright.config.ts served astro preview on port 5062.
specRef: SPEC 7.5 A-1 (criteria 2.1.1, 2.4.3); DECISIONS.md 'RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: done controls keep the focus' and 'RT-FIX-P3-residual-tools: an aria-disabled control ignores activation'
proposedFix: Apply the recorded pattern to each control: aria-disabled after hydration with the handler returning in that state. Where the control leaves the DOM (Draw the orbit), move the focus to a tabindex=-1 element inside the tool, as T4's keep counting does.

refute.citation: decisions/RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict.md (also in DECISIONS.md), '2026-10-17 RT-FIX-P3-follow-predict: done controls keep the focus': 'after hydration a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus: it carries aria-disabled=true instead of the HTML disabled attribute, and its handler does nothing in that state'. SPEC 7.5 A-1, criteria 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.4 and 2.4.3. The recorded rule supports the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: Read in my worktree, detached at b9b8504 and clean. The follow-predict entry opens with a general rule ('a control that its own press makes inactive keeps the focus'). 'This covers' then lists the controls that fix changed: Predict's Check and Show me; T8's vertices and focus button; T4's keep counting, which moves the focus to a tabindex=-1 counter section when the button goes; Step, Play to the end and Play on of T1, T5, T7, T8, T9 and T15. Its exceptions are named: before hydration (7.4); History and the step controls while a prediction freezes a board; Predict's answer fields once answered, 'since the answer is given from the two buttons and the focus is never in a field then'. None of the eight controls falls under an exception. The residual-tools entry 'an aria-disabled control ignores activation' governs the handlers of controls that are already aria-disabled. The board-a11y entry governs Board.svelte nodes only. Two earlier entries of 2026-10-10 call two of the eight 'disabled': P2-A3 ('removing the last node is refused (the button is disabled with the visible reason ...)') and P3-A5 (T7's table button 'Fire node k', 'disabled when the number is not positive'). Both predate the 2026-10-17 rule and say nothing about the attribute or the focus. No record covers T2's grow and showTotal, T5's game-B Step and Play to the end, T10's No rotation and Draw the orbit, or Challenge (the P1-A4 entries are silent). The source at the gate matches the locations given. T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1198 has rotateReset disabled={!api.hydrated || rotation === null}. At :996-1003, drawOrbit sits inside {#if orbit.kind === 'wait' ...}. Challenge.svelte:105-108 has a form with onsubmit, and its input and Check are disabled={!hydrated || met}. Enter in the input submits, so the focus is in the field when it is disabled, and the reason given for Predict's fields does not apply. All eight controls belong to phases 1 to 4. gate-G4.md (report commit 4e3e839, which names gate commit b9b8504) records no open item on this, and there is no earlier P4 round.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence permits dropping the focus and the recorded exceptions do not include these controls; R2 fails because the finding quotes the follow-predict rule correctly and that entry itself places 2.4.3 under A-1; R3 fails because every control is from phase 1 to 4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because the logged rule goes against the build, and the earlier P2-A3 and P3-A5 'disabled' entries cover only two of the eight controls and predate the rule (a partial refutation at most); R6 fails because nothing is on record.

title: Attacks 33 and 34: opening 'Show as table' on T1, T8 or T9 at 320 widens the whole tool frame past the viewport, so prose and controls stop reflowing
location: site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte. The .tool-frame grid has an implicit auto column. details.table-view is a grid item whose automatic minimum width is the table's min-content width, so the .bare fieldset's overflow-x: auto never takes effect. Seen with T01GameBoard, T08WeylExplorer and T09Kostant tables.
claim: With the table view open, the table's min-content width becomes the width of the frame's column. The tool title, figure, board, History and controls then run off-screen and the page scrolls sideways; the table has no scroll box of its own.
expected: SPEC 7.5 A-11: prose and controls reflow at 320, and two-dimensional content scrolls inside its own box. document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth should be 320 at a 320 viewport with the table open.
observed:
scrollWidth at 320 with the table open (320 in the default state):
- 585 on /tools/board/?z=1&g=E8&v=l&m=f&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1
- 338 on /tools/kostant/
- 385 on /tools/weyl/
- 361 on /modules/m1-mutation/ b4 (T1 on D4)
- 417 on /modules/m3-classification/ b6 (T1 on D4~)
Also M1 b5 and b10, M3 b8 and b12, M5 b2 to b5 and b13. Example: p.tool-title spans 16 to 401 px.
reproduction: npm ci --prefer-offline && npm run build && npx playwright test site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-05-p4-table-reflow.spec.ts (5 tests fail). The table is opened by keyboard: focus the summary, press Enter.

proposedFix: Give .tool-frame grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr), or min-width: 0 on details.table-view, so the existing overflow-x: auto of the fieldset scrolls the table inside its own box.

refute.citation: SPEC 7.5 A-11: 'Prose and controls reflow at 320 CSS pixels. A diagram that cannot (a wide orbit graph, the Weyl Explorer) scrolls inside its own box, which is the exception the criterion allows for two-dimensional content.' Also A-10, and 4.0 Small screens: 'Every tool is usable at a width of 320 CSS pixels.' The text supports the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: A-11 has no label and no qualifier for a view the reader opens. Its exception requires the two-dimensional part to scroll inside its own box, never the page. T8 is named in the exception, but only for scrolling inside its own box. 4.0 carries [D], and its 320-pixel sentence is the one the build departs from. The table view is required by A-10 and lives in ToolFrame (phase 1, P1-A2). T1 and T9 are phase 1 and T8 is phase 3. I searched the decisions fragments for table view, scroll, 320, minmax and reflow. P3-A5 gives T7's figure column minmax(0, 1fr) 'so that a long form never widens the page at 320 pixels (A-11)', which is the plan's own reading of A-11. P3-A3 records T5's scroll boxes. The RT-FIX-P3-layout entries cover Sources and the Predict field. No entry permits an open table view to widen the tool frame. gate-G4.md has no open item on this.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because A-11's exception covers a diagram that scrolls in its own box, not a page-level scroll that pushes prose and controls off-screen; R2 fails because expected reads A-11 and 4.0 correctly; R3 fails because the table view and T1, T8 and T9 are from phases 1 and 3; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because 4.0 is [D] but the build departs from its 320-pixel sentence and no record allows it; R6 fails because nothing is on record.

claim: An empty, fractional or worded answer is detected as invalid, but no text identifies the error. The live region is not written, predictResult stays empty and the field is not marked, so the reader who pressed Check neither sees nor hears anything.
expected: SPEC 7.5 targets WCAG 2.2 AA, which includes 3.3.1 Error Identification (A) and 4.1.3 Status Messages. SPEC 4.0: 'a polite live region announces each result'.
observed: M6 b7 (T11) with 'two', M7 b4 (T10) with '1.5' and M7 b4 with an empty field. After Enter on Check: live region texts [], data-out predictResult '', aria-invalid absent. Focus stays on Check and the board stays frozen.

refute.citation: SPEC 7.5, first sentence: 'Target: WCAG 2.2 level AA [S for the criteria].' Level AA includes 2.5.3 Label in Name (level A). The text supports the finding's expected.
refute.evidence: decisions/P3-A4.md '2026-10-10 P3-A4: placement by keys and buttons' records T6's visible labels 'a1 − 1', 'a1 + 1', 'a2 − 1' and 'a2 + 1' with the accessible names 'Move the point: number at node 1 minus 1', and so on. The entry is marked 'Plan.' and gives no 'what the specification left open'. It is not a section 10 default and not [D], since 7.5 carries no [D], so a builder's record cannot set aside the 7.5 target. P4-A3's turn entry (line 37) names the six visible labels and the group, not the aria-labels, and nothing records 'Raise the ring of node N'. Source at the gate: T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1116-1120 show the visible text 'Ring {focusLabel} up' and 'Ring {focusLabel} down' with aria-labels 'Raise the ring of node {focusLabel}' and 'Lower the ring of node {focusLabel}'. At :1171-1172 the visible text is 'Up' and 'Down' and the aria-labels are 'Turn about the horizontal axis, the top toward you' and '... away from you'. The lens's section 6 excludes only axe results of moderate or minor impact; this finding is a direct check, not an axe result. gate-G4.md has no record of this.
refute.reason: not refuted: R1 fails because no sentence narrows the AA target; R2 fails because 2.5.3 is a level A criterion inside that target; R3 fails because T6 is phase 3 and T10 is phase 4; R4 does not apply; R5 fails because P3-A4 records T6's names only as a plan choice, which cannot depart from 7.5 (7.5 is not [D] and no section 10 default applies), and nothing records T10's names; R6 fails because nothing is on record. The claimed minor matches 'a name' in the rubric.

title: Attack 6: a control rendered disabled before hydration (and with JavaScript off) looks exactly like the enabled control
location: site/src/components/board/ToolFrame.svelte:269-282 (.control sets color, background and border; .control:disabled changes only cursor); same pattern in T10GeometryStudio.svelte:1398-1415, T11FoldingBench.svelte:624-643 (.tab), Board.svelte:258-278 (.hit), History.svelte:87, Predict.svelte:167, T01GameBoard.svelte:770 and every other component's :disabled rule
claim: Every :disabled and [aria-disabled='true'] rule of the site changes only the cursor, and .control sets its own colour, background and border, overriding the browser's greying. So the disabled controls of the server markup, and the frozen boards after hydration, look the same as usable ones.
expected: SPEC 7.4: 'Controls are rendered with the disabled attribute, which the island removes when it hydrates, so a control never looks usable before it is.' A disabled control differs visibly from its enabled state.
observed: All 2021 buttons that hydration enables, on 22 routes, have the same computed colour, background, border colour, opacity, filter, text decoration and weight before and after hydration (as do 160 of 472 inputs; only selects and checkboxes grey). Example on /tools/geometry/: 'Root polytope', 'Coxeter plane', 'Copy link' and 'Download data' all read color rgb(26,26,26), background rgb(255,255,255), border rgb(26,26,26) solid, opacity 1, and give byte-identical element screenshots with JS off (disabled) and hydrated (enabled). The same holds on tools/fold (tab, reset, copyLink), M7 b1, M6 b8 and tools/board.
reproduction: From b9b8504 plus the reproducer files: npm ci; npm run build; PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<browsers> npx playwright test -c redteam/redteam-RT-06-playwright.config.ts site/tests/e2e/redteam-RT-06-disabled-look.spec.ts (5 failed, each listing controls with identical style and screenshots)
specRef: SPEC.md 7.4 'Without JavaScript' ('so a control never looks usable before it is'); 4.0 'Controls are present but disabled until the island has hydrated'; CONTRACTS 5.1 ToolFrame 'the control row rendered disabled until hydration'
proposedFix: Give :disabled and [aria-disabled='true'] one shared visible treatment in the control styles (for example reduced opacity or a dashed border, plus cursor), so it also covers frozen boards. Adopt the reproducer as a regression test.
